subject: FastCart throughput wobble — mitigation options + customer comms
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-22T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: FastCart throughput wobble — mitigation options + customer comms

Hi Elena / FastCart team,

We're seeing an intermittent throughput drop affecting your account starting ~11:05 PDT — overall QPS fell ~40% for a 7–10 minute window, p95 latency spiked ~3x during the same time. I attached a quick snapshot (20290522-fastcart-qps-snapshot.png) and linked the Grafana panel below.

Initial asks:
- Ben/infra: can you confirm whether the protective routing or instance-shedding policy kicked in for FastCart?
- Markus/eng: any recent kernel or batching changes that could surface as a throughput wobble? I attached the kernel change diff we've rolled to a subset of nodes.
- Marissa/product: do we want to authorize a temporary routing override (FastCart-specific) while we stabilize? That would let them keep steady throughput but increases unit cost.

Short-term mitigation options I'm proposing (we should pick 1–2 quickly):
1) Toggle routing override for FastCart for up to 4 hours (fastest).
2) Warm up KV cache and increase instance pool by adding 4 burst nodes (costly, but quick).
3) Roll back the batching/kernel change (risky if it's in-flight across many shards).

Customer comms: Elena — I'm drafting a one-paragraph note we can send once we decide. Prefer me to send a short status update now or wait until we have a definitive mitigation?

Links: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ops/fastcart-qps?from=now-1h
Jira: REDWOOD-JIRA-3187
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DF-4821

I marked this high priority. Please reply with what we can action in the next 15 minutes.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Reliability (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@fastcart.com>
Date: 2029-05-22T11:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastCart throughput wobble — mitigation options + customer comms

Jordan —

Thanks for flagging. Quick triage notes:
- Protective routing did partially engage for a subset of FastCart traffic between 11:06–11:13 PDT; we see ~15% of shards hit the soft-shed threshold.
- The batching hot-path shows elevated eviction rates at the same timestamps; looks like small objects are causing KV churn and hurting continuous batching efficiency.
- No hard OOMs. No downstream network errors.

Immediate actions I can take in the next 15m:
- Enable a FastCart routing override (no code change, runtime flag) — instant, but will increase token cost.
- Kick a KV warmup across their hot prefixes (will take ~8–12 minutes to see effect).

If we want to avoid the routing override, option (2) + a short TTL bump on hot keys should keep them within SLO and reduce shed after ~10m.

I'll stand by to flip the override if Marissa signs off. I'll also open a priority infra ticket and drop the logs into REDWOOD-JIRA-3187.

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the rapid triage. My read: prioritize customer stability first. Approve the routing override for up to 3 hours while Ben/infra warms the KV cache and Markus evaluates a short patch.

Operational asks for product/finance: we should track the incremental cost as a creditable incident (DF-4821) — I authorize temporary override for FastCart during this incident. Finance: please flag in the deal ledger post-incident for review.

Customer message (draft):
Hi Elena — we detected a transient throughput degradation that affected some of your requests. We've put a temporary routing override in place to stabilize traffic and are warming cache + pushing a targeted fix. Expect full normalization in ~30–90 minutes. We'll follow up once the root cause is confirmed and with any remediation steps.

Elena — if you want us to throttle instead of override, tell us now; otherwise we'll proceed with the override.

—Marissa
VP, Product

Subject: Re: FastCart throughput wobble — mitigation options + customer comms

Thanks Jordan / team. We saw the impact on our side (brief retries on checkout flows). The draft message looks good. Please proceed with the routing override — we prefer stability over throttled capacity.

Two asks from FastCart:
1) Can you confirm whether the override will route all traffic to the larger instances (we may see cost differences on our bill)?
2) If rollback is needed, we'd rather accept a short degraded model (smaller model) than a full rollback if that risks a broader regression.

Appreciate the quick response. Please keep us posted on ETA.

—Elena
Product Ops, FastCart

On Tue, May 22, 2029 at 11:40 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> All — thanks for the rapid triage. My read: prioritize customer stability first. Approve the routing override ...
>
Quick engineering update: the kernel diff attached does change batching window heuristics; rolling it back cluster-wide right now is non-trivial and risks additional churn. I do NOT recommend a full rollback as the immediate action.

Instead I can push a targeted soft-threshold tweak to the batching controller that reduces eviction pressure on small objects (REDWOOD-JIRA-3187-1). Estimated timeline: ~3 hours to test and stage a safe rollout with a canary. If Ben is enabling the routing override + KV warmup, we should see measurable improvement within ~20–30 minutes and full normalization in ~60–90 minutes.

I'll open REDWOOD-JIRA-3187-1 and link the PR; I'll update this thread once the canary passes.

—Markus
Senior Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
